## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kolaṁkolakathā* is a debate located in the twelfth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 12.6) in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The controversy examined in the text concerns whether an individual passing from family to family (*kolaṁkola*, a specific grade of stream-enterer) is fixed or assured (*niyata*) to that precise destiny [Bareau 1955].

According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits internal Pali text reuse with two other treatises in the *Kathāvatthu*, consisting of 22 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Its largest partners are the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), which accounts for 20 matching segments (with the longest matching sequence spanning §1.6–1.7 to §150.3–150.4), and the adjacent debate *Ekabījīkathā* (Kv 12.7) across two segments (§0.1–1.7) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports any cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists one translation in a modern language [SuttaCentral].
